expected_effect: Lower val_bpb by 0.002 to 0.006 versus the same-host pinned control at matched steps; step count within 3% of control (>= 2010 at 1800 s) because the added work is n_enc (3 at depth 6) broadcast multiply-adds on (B,T,n_embd) FP32 tensors per forward, no new matmuls, no new NEFF-heavy optimizer work (three extra 1-D AdamW tensors in an existing foreach group). Falsified if candidate bpb >= control bpb with steps inside the 10% comparability gate.
hypothesis: At the fixed 1800 s budget the control (2071 steps) already sits just under the ~2195-step epoch boundary, and every throughput-only variant that crossed it (2346-2716 steps) came back CONFOUNDED with worse BPB, so the remaining lever is loss-per-token, not steps. Zero-initialized U-Net style skip connections (modded-nanogpt records 8+: encoder block outputs added, LIFO, into the decoder blocks' residual stream through a learnable per-channel vector) shorten the gradient path to shallow features and let late blocks read early representations before they were overwritten. Because the skip vectors start at exactly zero the forward graph is bit-identical to the control at step 0 (same init RNG draws, no new torch RNG), so any BPB delta is causally attributable to the learned skips. Distinct from the existing input-dependent x0 gate (reads the embedding, not block outputs), the frozen block nudge, and the final-output pooling; the previous r1 proposal was judged architecturally bounded and non-duplicate and was returned only for (a) an incorrect optimizer-routing plan and (b) an over-broad data-wall claim, both fixed here.

STEP 3 (parameters): in GPT.__init__, after the blocks are built: if USE_UNET_SKIP and depth >= 2: self.unet_n_enc = depth // 2; self.unet_skip_gates = nn.ParameterList([nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(n_embd, dtype=torch.float32)) for _ in range(self.unet_n_enc)]); else: self.unet_n_enc = 0; self.unet_skip_gates = None. If init_weights iterates all parameters (per STEP 1d), add an explicit re-zero (p.zero_() under no_grad) of these vectors at the END of init_weights so they are exactly zero; if it only touches Linear/Embedding modules, add nothing but note it. Draw no torch RNG. STEP 4 (forward): in GPT.forward's block loop, keep the exact existing per-block call. Add before the loop: skips = []. After block i's output is assigned to x: if self.unet_n_enc and i < self.unet_n_enc: skips.append(x). Before calling block i for i >= self.unet_n_enc while skips is non-empty: j = i - self.unet_n_enc; x = x + self.unet_skip_gates[j].to(x.dtype) * skips.pop(). Do not alter any dtype, norm, x0, value-embedding or n-gram argument. Any existing training/eval helper that reimplements the block loop (e.g. a separate eval forward, causality check, or compiled wrapper) must receive the identical insertion or, if it calls GPT.forward, be left alone; record which. single_causal_change: One architecture change confined to train.py: new module-level toggle USE_UNET_SKIP (default True; env NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_UNET_SKIP='0' disables; CLI --unet-skip/--no-unet-skip; appended to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES so the checkpoint persists it and load_for_eval rebuilds the identical graph). When on, GPT owns n_enc = depth // 2 learnable FP32 vectors of shape (n_embd,) initialized to ZERO (nn.ParameterList self.unet_skip_gates). In GPT.forward the outputs of the first n_enc blocks are stacked; immediately before decoder block n_enc + j (j = 0..n_enc-1) the residual becomes x = x + unet_skip_gates[j] * (output of encoder block n_enc-1-j), i.e. the usual LIFO pairing. These vectors are EXPLICITLY appended to the existing gate/conv AdamW parameter list inside setup_optimizer (the group that already holds the 1-D gate tensors), inheriting its lr/betas/wd; they are never placed in the scalar group nor in Muon. Nothing else changes: block-call signature, all norm/dtype policies, x0 gate, value embeddings, n-gram VE, optimizer hyperparameters, schedule, data, evaluator all untouched.
